newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Reynolds upbeat despite poor debut.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Reynolds upbeat despite poor debut.

text.p: Shares of aluminium maker Reynolds Philippine Corp made a lacklustre debut on Thursday but the company and the stock's underwriter said the poor showing did not reflect the firm's positive fundamentals.

"There's nothing wrong with Reynolds. It's fundamentally strong. It was just affected by the downtrend in the local market," said Eleuterio Coronel, chief operating officer of All Asia Capital and Trust Corp, the issue's lead underwriter.

The initial public offering (IPO) of Reynolds, the country's only integrated aluminium manufacturer, closed at its offering price of 4.55 pesos, but early trading saw the stock tumble to as low as 4.05.
"Why should you sell below offering? Just let this week pass and the fundamentals of the firm will manifest itself," Coronel told reporters.

Reynolds officials said recent reports in local newspapers that the firm had cut its earnings forecast for this year to 301 million pesos from 332 million -- and that the downgrade could reflect poor fundamentals -- had also affected the issue.

Chief financial officer Jorge Navarra said the 332 million peso forecast, made last September, was only a preliminary estimate. Since the IPO was delayed to February from late 1996, the forecast had to be revised to reflect interest charges.

Reynolds' IPO was intended to raise funds to reduce its interest expenses, president Jaime Gonzales said. Coronel said 92 percent of the 1.082 billion peso proceeds from the IPO will be used for debt repayment.

Pamela Anday, analyst at Philippine Asia Equity, said there was a lot of confusion on where the company's profits will come from this year. "Earnings from operations this year will be good but not quite brilliant," she said.
Reynolds officials said the firm's prospects remain bright.
"We expect to ride the boom in construction and healthy growth in the local beverage and liquor industries," said Navarra.

All Asia Securities said in a study it expected local demand for aluminium products to grow in tandem with the economy. Reynolds' rated capacity is expected to increase by 13 percent to 20,250 tonnes this year after an expansion of its plant, begun in 1991, is completed this year.

"Over the next three years demand for aluminium curtain walls is expected to increase as 52 new high-storeyed buildings are expected to be set up in the country," said Ernesto Versoza, president of Fuji Reynolds Fabrication Corp, a joint venture between Reynolds and Fujisash Co Ltd.
Reynolds is also expected to benefit from the growth of the local food and beverage sectors.

The firm plans to spend between $25 and $30 million on the production of aluminium can stock, the raw material in the manufacture of aluminium cans. The project is expected to cater to the needs of brewers San Miguel Corp and Asia Brewery Inc.

San Miguel's can unit is increasing the 450-million unit capacity of its plant while Asia Brewery plans to build its own plant. Both plants will have a total capacity of between 1.6 billion and 1.7 billion units annually which, however, would account for just 12 percent of total annual demand for beverage cans, Gonzales said.
